claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known grant compliance review weakness remaining in scope for the initial rollout.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not override the disclosure policy for a named exposed weak segment.
Under the policy text, rollout controls and monitoring mitigate the weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or exposure is covered by reviewed risk acceptance.
Because admissible evidence shows neither exclusion nor approved risk acceptance, certification is not policy-compliant on the current record.
Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring supports good practice but does not supply the missing policy predicate for certification.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance that explicitly addresses grant compliance review exposure and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
Evidence that the initial rollout excludes the affected grant compliance review segment.
Evidence that the named-use-case limitation was resolved before launch.
Launch disclosure materials showing the material limitation was disclosed in accordance with policy.
specific_concerns: The affected grant compliance review segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout control is random by cohort and does not exclude the affected use case.
The risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not address the exposed grant compliance review segment.
Policy requires either resolving the material limitation, disclosing it, or covering exposure with approved risk acceptance before launch.
A 6% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring do not satisfy the policy when the affected segment remains exposed.
unsupported_claims: The certification decision is compliant based on aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one incidents, limited rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring alone.
The certification defense is supportable, even weakly, under the stated disclosure policy without approved risk acceptance or exclusion of the affected use case.
